```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Scope and provenance

This newly authored R Markdown companion summarizes the supplied Quetta extract. It is not an original uploaded analysis file. It retains the existing derived indicators rather than reclassifying respondents. The statistical tests in the separate report are not recomputed here. Survey weights produce descriptive totals; no complex-survey standard errors are estimated.

```{r import}
d <- read_dta(params$data_path)
d <- d[substr(as.character(d$PCode), 1, 2) == "41", ]
stopifnot(nrow(d) == 9652, all(is.finite(d$Weights)), all(d$Weights > 0))
age_names <- c("0–9", "10–19", "20–29", "30–39", "40–49",
               "50–59", "60–69", "70–79", "80–89", "90+")
d <- d %>% mutate(
  age_band = factor(as.integer(age_group), levels = 1:10, labels = age_names),
  settlement = factor(as.integer(Region), levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Rural", "Urban")),
  sex = factor(as.integer(gender), levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female"))
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(Respondents = nrow(d), Weighted_population = sum(d$Weights)))
```

# Economic activity

Participation below divides labor force by all selected respondents, including children. It is not a conventional working-age labor force participation rate. Unemployment divides unemployed respondents by the labor force.

```{r activity}
summary <- d %>% summarise(
  population = sum(Weights),
  employed = sum(Weights * employed),
  unemployed = sum(Weights * unemployed),
  labor_force = sum(Weights * labor_force),
  outside_labor_force = sum(Weights * not_in_labor_force)
) %>% mutate(
  participation_percent = 100 * labor_force / population,
  unemployment_percent = 100 * unemployed / labor_force,
  unclassified = population - labor_force - outside_labor_force
)
knitr::kable(summary, digits = 2)
stopifnot(sum(d$employed) == 2121, sum(d$unemployed) == 98)
by_age <- d %>% group_by(age_band) %>% summarise(
  respondents = n(), population = sum(Weights),
  employed = sum(Weights * employed),
  unemployed = sum(Weights * unemployed),
  labor_force = sum(Weights * labor_force), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(by_age, digits = 1)
ggplot(by_age, aes(age_band, employed)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#252528") +
  labs(x = "Age group", y = "Weighted people", title = "Employment by age") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Settlement and gender

```{r demographic-comparison}
comparison <- d %>% group_by(settlement, sex) %>% summarise(
  respondents = n(), population = sum(Weights),
  labor_force = sum(Weights * labor_force),
  unemployed = sum(Weights * unemployed), .groups = "drop") %>% mutate(
  participation_percent = ifelse(population > 0, 100 * labor_force / population, NA_real_),
  unemployment_percent = ifelse(labor_force > 0, 100 * unemployed / labor_force, NA_real_))
knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 2)
ggplot(comparison, aes(settlement, participation_percent, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#252528", "#a78bfa")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Labor force / full population (%)", fill = "Gender") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Education and marital status

Education labels reproduce the supplied project mapping of S4C9 codes 1–7; they have not been independently verified against the PBS codebook. Missing or unmapped values are retained as unclassified.

```{r education-and-marital}
education_names <- c("Unclassified", "No formal education", "Below primary", "Primary",
                     "Middle", "Matric", "Intermediate", "Graduation")
ed <- as.integer(d$edu_level)
ed[is.na(ed) | !(ed %in% 1:7)] <- 0L
d$education_label <- factor(ed, levels = 0:7, labels = education_names)
education_table <- d %>% group_by(education_label) %>% summarise(
  respondents = n(), weighted_population = sum(Weights), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(education_table, digits = 1)
marital <- as.integer(d$marital_status)
marital[is.na(marital) | !(marital %in% 1:4)] <- 0L
d$marital_label <- factor(marital, levels = 0:4,
  labels = c("Unclassified", "Never married", "Married", "Widow / widower", "Divorced"))
knitr::kable(d %>% group_by(marital_label) %>% summarise(
  respondents = n(), weighted_population = sum(Weights), .groups = "drop"), digits = 1)
```

# Interpretation and limitations

The extract is cross-sectional and specific to the 2020–21 survey geography. Survey weights do not resolve classification errors or supply uncertainty estimates. The 3,143 respondents aged 0–9 are not flagged as in or outside the labor force by the supplied indicators. Associations cannot establish causal effects. Small groups require particular caution.
